business_problem: DLG needed a way to turn live trade-fair presentations into written, barrier-free, multilingual content so international attendees and people with hearing impairments could follow sessions without relying on traditional simultaneous interpreters.
solution_summary: DLG deployed transcribbyAI from Deutsche Telekom MMS as a browser-based AI simultaneous interpretation application for its trade fairs. Organizers run the application on a computer that receives the live event audio stream; a microphone connects through a standard audio cable, or a recorded audio file can be played in as the source. transcribbyAI uses Microsoft Azure AI language models to perform real-time speech recognition, speech synthesis, and translation, automatically detecting the source language and translating output into more than 100 languages. During pauses it corrects capitalization and punctuation, masks inappropriate expressions with symbols, and distinguishes speakers by voice color. The resulting text is delivered to large stage screens and to mobile devices through QR-code access. The source does not name a dedicated storage product, but it does state that transcripts can be exported for further processing. The solution was operated on German servers with certified IT security and GDPR-compliant hosting, and Telekom MMS ran it across five stages in parallel at Agritechnica.

data_flow: A presentation audio stream reaches a browser-based transcribbyAI session from a connected microphone or from a played-back audio file. transcribbyAI uses Microsoft Azure language models for real-time recognition and translation, then returns corrected subtitles and multilingual text to stage screens or QR-code mobile views, with transcript export available for further processing.
integration_points: Connected microphone via standard audio cable
business_outcome: DLG expanded the reach of its trade fairs with multilingual, barrier-free access to presentations, created additional value for attendees and partners, and reduced the cost of hiring simultaneous translators.
